detection_signals.reasoning: A single source IP (198.51.100.77) performed 20 failed login attempts across 8 distinct usernames (including root, oracle, and test) in just 0.9 seconds. This rapid, automated targeting of multiple user accounts from one IP represents a brute force/password spraying attack that warrants escalation.

assessment_at_capture.rationale: The incident shows a deliberate, rapid brute-force attack from a known malicious IP (198.51.100.77) targeting multiple accounts (root, oracle, test) within a fraction of a second. Crucially, the attack resulted in 3 successful logins during the burst from the same timeframe, indicating a potential successful account compromise.

correlation.intel_summary: The threat-intel lookup for the single source IP involved in the failed logins (198.51.100.77) returned a 'malicious' reputation categorized as a scanner/brute-force source range.
correlation.enrichment_notes: The reputation lookup confirms that the primary source IP (198.51.100.77) is flagged as malicious (associated with host-scanning and brute-force activity). This significantly increases the concern level, as the 20 failed login attempts are not just random noise or a misconfigured script, but originate from a known malicious infrastructure targeting multiple accounts (root, oracle, test, etc.). Furthermore, the fact that there were 3 successful logins in the same burst makes this a high-priority potential credential compromise incident.

status_history.note: fanning out to Containment and On-Call
